codes.description: The customer carries a do-not-contact flag. Suppresses every automated contact treatment and is re-checked immediately before dispatch, so a flag set after the decision still prevents the send.
The customer is flagged as vulnerable or in an assistance programme, so collection contact is held pending the vulnerability-safe treatment path.
Policy forbids automated contact for this customer; only collector-initiated action is permitted. The A§54 worked example: policy forbids, optimization prefers SMS, result is no SMS.
A legal case is active on the account, so collections contact is suspended while the legal process runs.
An open complaint places the account on hold; contact resumes only when the complaint is resolved.
An insolvency or bankruptcy notification was received for the customer, which removes the account from normal collections contact.
The customer is recorded as deceased; all contact is suppressed and the account follows the bereavement process.
The account matched the eligibility conditions of the selected strategy. Emitted on every decision that reached a strategy, so an explanation always states which gate was passed.

No ACTIVE strategy's eligibility matched this context, so the decision is INELIGIBLE and no strategy is attributed. Usually means a coverage gap rather than a healthy exclusion — a rising count is a signal to review strategy eligibility.
The selected channel is usable for this customer: contact details exist for it and no constraint removed it.
The channel a treatment needs is unusable — no contact detail on file, or the detail failed validation — so the treatment was not a candidate.
The account is current (0 DPD, nothing overdue), so no collections strategy applies.
The account is closed or written off and is out of scope for collections treatment.
Early-stage delinquency with a low risk profile: no broken promises, contactable, modest exposure. Receives the light-touch treatment ladder.
Early-stage delinquency with adverse indicators (broken promises, low contactability or high exposure). Escalates faster than the low-risk segment.
Later-stage delinquency where the treatment ladder moves from reminders to collector contact and formal notices.
The catch-all segment: the subject matched no earlier segment. Every subject lands in exactly one segment, so "unsegmented" is never a silent state.
Days past due is between 1 and 30 inclusive.
Days past due is between 31 and 60 inclusive — the A§55 / D§8 worked example condition (dpd 35).
Days past due is between 61 and 90 inclusive.
Days past due is over 90.
The customer's derived contactability is HIGH, so a self-service digital or SMS treatment is likely to reach them (A§58).
The customer's derived contactability is LOW or UNCONTACTABLE, which favours letter or collector treatment over messaging.
The rule set permits SMS for this subject: mobile contact is available, no policy narrowing applies and the SMS frequency budget is not exhausted (A§58).
No payment arrangement is active on the account, so collection contact is appropriate (A§58).
An arrangement is active and being honoured, so contact is suppressed — chasing a customer who is paying to plan is the fastest way to break the plan.
A promise to pay is open and not yet due, so the account waits for the promise date rather than being contacted again.
One or more promises were broken in the last 90 days, which disqualifies the light-touch treatments and escalates the ladder.
The PAYMENT_PROPENSITY model returned a score and its band was used in the decision. The exact score and band are in the decision trace; the code records that the model participated (A§56/A§58).
Payment propensity fell in the high band: a reminder is likely to be sufficient, so the cheapest effective channel is preferred.
Payment propensity fell in the low band, which favours earlier collector contact over further automated reminders.

A model call failed or timed out and the strategy's `onError: DEFAULT` substituted its `defaultScore`. Recorded so a substituted score is never mistaken for a real one, and so the substitution rate is countable.

The post-selection guard re-validated the chosen treatment against the policy snapshot and rejected it, so the decision is NO_ACTION and nothing is dispatched. Its presence means the pipeline tried to select something policy forbids — a bug to be investigated, never an expected outcome (A§54, CLAUDE.md hard rule 2).
A POLICY rule set FORBID_CHANNEL narrowing removed this channel from consideration before selection.
A policy constraint suppressed every treatment for this subject, so the decision is SUPPRESSED. The specific POLICY code accompanies this one.
Every candidate treatment was filtered out by policy, constraints or channel eligibility, leaving nothing to select, so the decision is NO_ACTION.

The decision context could not be assembled — an upstream service failed or timed out — so no decision was taken. Fail closed: a partial context is never decided on (also the A§20 error code returned to the caller).

The pre-dispatch customer-policy re-check could not be completed, so the treatment is SUPPRESSED rather than sent on the assumption that the previous answer still holds. Fail closed by design (DEC-16).
Dispatch fell outside the channel's permitted local contact window from the published guardrail configuration. The treatment is rescheduled to the next window opening rather than dropped.
Sending would exceed a contact frequency cap for the channel or across all channels in its rolling window, so the treatment is SUPPRESSED.
The channel provider rejected the dispatch after retries, so the treatment is FAILED. Distinguishes a delivery failure from a platform decision not to contact.
